title: Phase Transition from Random Features to Fully Trainable Networks
why_read: A dense theoretical analysis of neural network trainability tradeoffs, valuable mainly to specialists in approximation theory rather than general practitioners.
analysis: This paper studies networks that mix fixed random features with trainable parameters, and mathematically characterizes how performance improves as more of the network becomes trainable. It finds a 'phase transition' pattern where a small trainable fraction captures most of the benefit, with precise bounds derived under specific statistical assumptions. The math is rigorous but narrow, focused on two-layer and some deeper networks under idealized conditions like polynomial spectral decay. This is mostly of interest to researchers in learning theory or numerical analysis rather than applied machine learning engineers.
